prompt: A cube has surface area $216$ square units. What is its **volume**?
hint: Volume needs the edge length. Work backward from the surface area to one face, and then from that face to the edge.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Start with a smaller cube: surface area $24$ means each face is $24 \div 6 = 4$, the edge is $2$, and the volume is $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$.
Volume needs the edge length. Work backward from the surface area to one face, and then from that face to the edge.
One face has area $216 \div 6 = 36$, so the edge is $6$ because $6 \times 6 = 36$. Now compute $6 \times 6 \times 6$.
$6 \times 6 \times 6 = 216$, so the volume of the cube is $216$ cubic units.

explanation: A cube has $6$ equal faces, so one face has area $216 \div 6 = 36$ square units.
A face is a square, so the edge is the number whose square is $36$, which is $6$.
The volume of a cube is edge times edge times edge: $6 \times 6 \times 6$.
Multiply in two steps to keep it simple: $6 \times 6 = 36$, and $36 \times 6 = 216$.
The volume is $216$ cubic units. It is a coincidence that this matches the surface area number.
